title: Degreewise invertibility of explicit principal Cech regrouping
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $r\in\mathbb N$, $f:\operatorname{Fin}r\to A$, and $F$ an integer-indexed cochain complex of module sheaves on $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Write $C_p(F)$ for the product column of [def-sc-principal-cech-columns] and $T^n(F)=\prod_{J\ne\varnothing}\Gamma(D(\prod_{j\in J}f_j),F^{n+1-|J|})$ for the explicit terms of [def-sc-principal-open-alternating-total]. Let $B$ be an integer-indexed bicomplex of $A$-modules and let $e_p:B^{p,\bullet}\cong C_p(F)$ be arbitrary isomorphisms of vertical complexes. Define $R^n:(\operatorname{Tot}B)^n\to T^n(F)$ by the diagonal coproduct universal property [def-sp-double-complex-total]: on the $(p,q)$ summand, where $p+q=n$, apply $e_p$ in degree $q$, project to the coordinate $J$ if $|J|=p+1$, transport along $q=n+1-|J|$, and set all other coordinates to zero. Then every $R^n$ is an isomorphism of $A$-modules. No compatibility of the $e_p$ with horizontal differentials is required.

proof.text: Evaluate each product column in degree q. Mathlib preservation of products by HomologicalComplex.eval makes piComparison invertible. Construct rowRetract by restricting the explicit subset coordinates to the row, transporting their degrees, and composing with the inverse product comparison. Projection extensionality proves that row inclusion followed by its retraction is the identity, that inclusion followed by another row retraction is zero, and that retraction followed by inclusion is the coordinate mask for that row.

Let rows be the finite image of J ↦ |J|-1 on nonempty subsets of Fin r. Define the inverse regrouping map as the sum over rows of rowRetract, followed by the inverse column isomorphism e_p in degree n-p and the canonical diagonal total inclusion. For regrouping followed by this inverse, use total.hom_ext and the same-row and different-row identities; if p is not in rows, its product index is empty and its evaluated column, hence the source summand, is zero. For the other composite, use the coordinate mask and sum_eq_single at |J|-1. This includes r=0, arbitrary integer total degrees, and arbitrary F, without horizontal compatibility or boundedness.
